symptom: After `mxcli marketplace update`, a local module's cross-module association into the updated module is gone; replaying it from `--save-edits` brings the association back but every stored link is NULL (follow-up to mendixlabs/mxcli#1502). With the association's member access still in the local entity's rule, `mx check` reports CE1613 "The selected association 'MyFirstModule.Config_Account' no longer exists." at Access rule of entity 'MyFirstModule.Config'.
cause: DROP MODULE -> DeleteEntity cascades into other domain models and removes CrossAssociations whose `Child` names a dropped entity; the FROM entity's MemberAccess (by name) is left dangling. A replay re-creates the association with a fresh GUID, and the runtime keys associations on the GUID (`mendixsystem$association.id`), so it is a new association to the database. Fixed by `CaptureDependentAssociations` (before the drop) + `RestoreDependentAssociations` (after ApplyIdentities) in cmd/mxcli/marketplace/dependents.go, which splice the stored element back verbatim when the new version still has the target entity and report it lost otherwise; the update gate no longer refuses over them.
insight: Splicing the stored element back is safe here because the owning module is untouched by the update: the element's ParentPointer still names the FROM entity's unchanged $ID, and its own $ID and GUID are already the project's, so plain UpdateRawUnit keeps them byte-for-byte (asserted; canon did not re-pair). The GUID test needs a subject with GUID != $ID — mxcli mints them equal, so a re-mint from $ID passes unnoticed; a control that re-mints was caught only after the subject's GUID was set apart. The live measurement is cheap with `run --local --ensure-db` on testdata/expr-checker: the association column has a real FK, so seed system$user + administration$account + the config row; control = unchanged reboot (4242 kept), fixed = 4242 kept, replay = NULL. `mx check` alone would not have shown the data loss — the replayed model checks clean.
